summary: Distinct FidelityManager boundary remains after active PR #274: caller-supplied PolicyConfig is dereferenced and operated on before any plain-table/metatable or primitive-number preflight. A top-level config __index can execute during new(config) copyConfig before validation, and evaluatePolicy(customConfig) reaches validateConfig where maxRegisteredEntities comparison/math.floor and later cross-field arithmetic/comparisons occur before config-wide scalar type validation. PR #274 hardens PolicyInputs/nowSeconds but leaves validateConfig/copyConfig unchanged. Prefer consuming this in the active HG-BACKFILL-FIDELITY lane if its primary/reviewer agree PolicyConfig is part of the plain/no-execute contract; otherwise document PolicyConfig as explicitly trusted code-owned configuration rather than silently leaving the boundary ambiguous.
evidence: PR #274 head 5251998d: validateConfig begins with config.maxRegisteredEntities >= 1 / < math.huge / math.floor before any type(config) or getmetatable(config) guard.
PR #274 head 5251998d: copyConfig reads every supplied config field; FidelityManager.new(config) calls copyConfig before validateConfig, so hostile top-level __index executes before rejection.
PR #274 adds metatable-free/primitive guards for PolicyInputs and nowSeconds only; its current patch does not alter PolicyConfig validation/copying.
Current fidelity_manager, fidelity_manager_determinism, and fidelity_manager_rejected_step_atomicity suites inspected by this miner contain no hostile PolicyConfig/no-execute regression.
